questions: How many devices did you measure, and how many showed high-field supercurrent? Table S1 and Sec. F answer this in part (four moiré junctions, two with high-field pockets, plus the non-moiré junction of Sec. H); could you reconcile this with "multiple additional devices" on p. 3, and say how many cooldowns each device had?
Why were the others set aside? Sec. F gives the length of GH3 and GH4 as the reason; were other junctions on the same stacks (Fig. S1a shows several contacts per mesa) measured and not listed?
Which ranges of field, density and bias did you measure beyond the ones shown, in particular the hole-side minibands (n/ns < −1) at high field, fields between 6 and 8 T, and negative field?
What does the second-best dataset look like, for example interference patterns like Fig. 2c at other densities in the minibands, and for GH2 beyond Fig. S13c?
How was the 3447 Ω series resistance calibrated, does it stay the same at 4 to 6 T, and how do Fig. 2a and Fig. 3e look before it is subtracted?
For the pockets in Fig. 2a, could you show dV/dI out to a bias of order 2∆/e, so a reader can see each pocket's zero-voltage branch next to any finite-bias resonances?

Ben Shalom et al. (your Ref. 20) attribute similar high-field pockets to near-edge Andreev states. What in your data separates bulk Hofstadter-band trajectories from near-edge states, and could the Fraunhofer-envelope analysis of Fig. S9 be applied to Fig. 2c and Fig. S11?
How were the colour limits of Fig. 3d and the 20 mS cutoff of Fig. S18c-d chosen, and does the match between 1/R and ⟨v²⟩/vF² hold with other limits or with the 0.17 threshold of p. 7?
